manifest.name: dsh-theme-atlas
manifest.description: Atlas: six material skins for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI — one token engine derives the 119 --dsw-* alias tokens per appearance, light and dark, switched in-app. No images, no host route.
manifest.author: John-20260101

scripts.test: node scripts/verify.mjs && node tests/assets.mjs && node tests/host.mjs && node tests/client.mjs

bundle.text:
# dsh-theme-atlas bundle patch.
#
# Contributes one host row. The theme itself is browser-side: it ships through
# the `dsh.client` manifest in package.json, so this row only has to exist for
# the bundle to be listed, enabled and unloaded as a unit.
#
# A patch replaces the targeted row's whole `config`; only additive `insert`
# rows appear here, never an override of a shipped row.
- insert:
    - id: theme-atlas
      name: dsh-theme-atlas

readme.text:
**Six material skins for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI. One token engine, light and dark, switched from inside the app — no images, no host route.**

[中文说明](./README.zh.md) · [Theme document](./docs/themes.md) · [Palette reference](./docs/palettes.md) · [Image sizes](./docs/images.md)

Atlas is a theme *pack*, not a single recolour. Each skin declares six input colours per appearance; the engine derives the 119 `--dsw-*` alias tokens the Web shell reads from them, then measures the result. Six skins × two appearances = twelve palettes that all share the same semantic rules, so a state that reads in light mode reads in dark.

Every skin is painted with CSS: a signature gradient wash, selection colour and focus ring. The pack ships no bitmap and registers no plugin-owned route, so it works on exactly the same shells with or without a host `webServer` service. The three Leshan photograph skins that used to live here now ship separately as [`dsh-theme-leshan`](https://github.com/John-20260101/dsh-theme-leshan).

| **赤陶 Terracotta** | 未上釉的陶土 · 砂 / Unglazed clay and sand | `#AE5229` / `#E08C5F` | 14.9:1 / 15.0:1 | [light](./assets/screenshots/02-terracotta-light-1600x1000.jpg) |
| **极光 Aurora** | 极地冰晶 · 夜光 / Polar ice and night glow | `#16758F` / `#55D6D2` | 15.5:1 / 16.3:1 | [light](./assets/screenshots/03-aurora-light-1600x1000.jpg) |
| **深海 Abyss** | 深海蓝 · 微光 / Deep water and faint light | `#1B58B4` / `#5B8DEF` | 15.9:1 / 16.1:1 | [light](./assets/screenshots/04-abyss-light-1600x1000.jpg) |
| **樱雾 Sakura Mist** | 薄樱 · 雾面 / Thin blossom on mist | `#B1436B` / `#E78BA8` | 15.1:1 / 15.8:1 | [light](./assets/screenshots/05-sakura-light-1600x1000.jpg) |

Dark examples: [Aurora dark](./assets/screenshots/07-aurora-dark-1600x1000.jpg) · [Paper dark](./assets/screenshots/08-paper-dark-1600x1000.jpg). Full palettes, token tables and measured contrast live in [docs/palettes.md](./docs/palettes.md).

readme.section: or the prebuilt tarball (no build step)
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/John-20260101/dsh-theme-atlas/releases/latest/download/dsh-theme-atlas.tgz
```

Desktop: **插件 → 添加插件**, paste `github:John-20260101/dsh-theme-atlas`, enable it, then reload the window if the shell asks.

The plugin is a normal bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle` + a `cordis.patch.yml`, so `dsh plugin add` can load it. There is no build step to approve — `client.js` ships prebuilt.

- Click the **Atlas** pill at the bottom-right of the window, or press <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> to cycle.
- The choice is browser-local (`localStorage: dsh.theme-atlas.skin`), so different browsers can run different skins.
- “隐藏此钮” hides the pill (`dsh.theme-atlas.rail`); <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> keeps working, and clearing that key brings the pill back.
- Light/dark still belongs to the shell’s own **Appearance** setting — Atlas has both palettes and never overrides your preference.

1. **Token layer.** On load it calls `ctx.theme.overrideTokens('dsh-theme-atlas', layer)`, where `layer` maps every `--dsw-*` alias token to a `{ light, dark }` pair. Switching a skin replaces that layer; unloading the plugin removes it. On a shell without the theme service it falls back to a scoped stylesheet with the same values.
2. **Signature wash.** One small plugin-owned stylesheet adds the skin’s page gradient, selection colour and focus ring, keyed by `html[data-dsh-atlas]`. No layout is touched and no image is loaded.
3. **Skin rail.** A shadow-DOM panel so no shell rule can reach it, keyboard reachable, removed with the plugin.

On unload the plugin removes its attributes, custom properties, style tags, rail and token layer — the page returns to the shell’s own painting. Nothing else is written: no host settings document, no files, no network calls.

| Set | Size | Count | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Storefront screenshots | 1600×1000 (16:10) | 8 | [`assets/screenshots/`](./assets/screenshots) |
| Contact sheet | 2400×1350 (16:9) | 1 | [`assets/screenshots/`](./assets/screenshots) |
| Key art | 1536×1024 (3:2) | 6 | [`assets/keyart/`](./assets/keyart) |
| Storefront icon | 1024, 512, 180 square | 3 | [`assets/`](./assets) |

These are documentation and storefront images only — no skin reads them. Sizes, display guidance and regeneration commands are specified in [docs/images.md](./docs/images.md); `screenshots.json` points the storefront at the eight UI shots.

- DeepSeek Harness Web **0.2.0-rc.1 … 0.2.x** (`dsh.bundle` + `dsh.client`).
- Works in the official Desktop app and in `dsh web`; needs a browser with `color-mix()` (Chromium 111+, Safari 16.2+).
- No host service is required: the bundle row is inert, and the theme applies with or without the theme service (the fallback layer still applies both palettes).

```sh
npm install
npm run verify   # build + token completeness + WCAG gates
npm run shots    # re-render every image at the documented size
```

Source layout: `src/color.mjs` (colour maths), `src/tokens.mjs` (the 119-name contract), `src/skins.mjs` (six skins, six inputs per appearance), `src/derive.mjs` (role derivation), `src/runtime.mjs` (tokens, rail, unload cleanup), `index.js` (the inert bundle row). `client.js` is generated — edit `src/` and run `npm run build`.
Adding a skin is one row in `src/skins.mjs`; run `npm run verify` and the contrast gate tells you whether the two new palettes hold up.

MIT. Palette names and copy are original to this repository; the `--dsw-*` token names belong to DeepSeek Harness. The Leshan photographs are not part of this package — they ship with [`dsh-theme-leshan`](https://github.com/John-20260101/dsh-theme-leshan).
